system_overview: This specification is a modified version of the spanning tree algorithm in which the edge set is not a declared constant but is instead defined as a randomly chosen set of edges joining the nodes. This allows the model checker to test the spanning tree algorithm on a randomly generated graph each time it runs, making it easy to check the algorithm's correctness across a variety of different graph topologies without manually specifying each one.
actors_and_components: The system operates on an undirected graph with a fixed set of nodes but a randomly generated edge set. There is a single designated root node. The algorithm is the same centralized spanning tree algorithm: in each step, it nondeterministically selects a node and one of its neighbors, then updates the node's distance and parent if an improvement is possible.
state_variables: The system maintains two mappings over all nodes: (1) a parent function that maps each node to its parent in the spanning tree (the root and unreachable nodes map to themselves), and (2) a distance function that maps each node to a natural number representing its computed distance from the root. The edge set is defined (not a variable) but is computed randomly at initialization time.
initial_state: Every node's parent is set to itself. The root node's distance is set to 0. All other nodes' distances are set to the maximum cardinality constant. The edge set is determined by randomly choosing, for each node, a subset of other nodes to connect to, and forming two-element edge sets from those choices.
actions: Same as the base spanning tree algorithm: choose a node and one of its graph neighbors such that the neighbor's distance plus one is strictly less than the node's current distance. Choose a new distance for the node that is strictly less than its current distance but at least the neighbor's distance plus one. Update the node's distance and parent accordingly.
safety_properties: When the algorithm terminates, the postcondition holds: for every node, one of three cases applies: (1) it is the root with distance 0 and parent equal to itself; (2) it is unreachable with maximum distance, parent equal to itself, and all neighbors also unreachable; or (3) it has a distance between 1 and the maximum minus one, its parent is a graph neighbor, and its distance equals its parent's distance plus one. The safety property asserts this postcondition always holds upon termination. Additionally, a type correctness invariant checks that the parent mapping goes from nodes to nodes, the distance mapping goes from nodes to natural numbers, and all edges are two-element subsets of nodes.
liveness_properties: The postcondition is eventually reached. This is ensured by weak fairness on the transition relation.
model_bounds: The set of nodes, the root node, and the maximum cardinality constant are declared as constants. A typical model configuration uses six nodes. The maximum cardinality must be a natural number at least as large as the number of nodes. On a few test runs with six nodes, the model checker took an average of slightly more than 30 seconds.
additional_assumptions: The edge generation uses a non-standard random element selection mechanism that does not obey the normal rules of mathematical equality (evaluating the same expression twice may yield different results). This is a deliberate hack for testing purposes. The root must be a member of the node set.
